title: Nghệ thuật công và phản đối · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support allowing public funding for art that offends some taxpayers, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Dạng discuss yêu cầu giải thích riêng vì sao mỗi phía tin lập trường của mình rồi đưa phán đoán của người viết. Trong bài này, cân nhắc trọng tâm là: Tài trợ ngoài thị trường giúp tác phẩm thách thức quan niệm số đông tồn tại. Ví dụ lịch sử bị bỏ qua giải thích vì sao gây khó chịu có thể gắn với giá trị thảo luận. Quyết định độc lập giảm can thiệp chính trị; minh bạch và quyền phản biện giữ trách nhiệm công. Không nên dùng tự do nghệ thuật để miễn mọi giải trình ngân sách.
outline.content: Supporters argue that public support can protect artistic experimentation from purely commercial pressures. Opponents respond that public institutions can lose trust if they dismiss all criticism as hostility to artistic freedom. I favour protecting challenging art from a taxpayer veto, but agree with opponents that public institutions owe an explanation of artistic value and selection procedures rather than an automatic defence of controversy.

paragraphs: Supporters argue that public support can protect artistic experimentation from purely commercial pressures. Opponents respond that public institutions can lose trust if they dismiss all criticism as hostility to artistic freedom. I favour protecting challenging art from a taxpayer veto, but agree with opponents that public institutions owe an explanation of artistic value and selection procedures rather than an automatic defence of controversy.

Public support can protect artistic experimentation from purely commercial pressures. Art can challenge dominant assumptions precisely because it is not designed to please every consumer. A controversial exhibition could encourage discussion of an overlooked historical injustice. Freedom from immediate sales pressure can create room for difficult subjects, including accounts of history that audiences or sponsors might prefer to avoid. An exhibition may have value because it challenges a comfortable historical account, but controversy alone does not establish artistic quality or justify public expenditure.

Public institutions can lose trust if they dismiss all criticism as hostility to artistic freedom. Funding bodies can lose legitimacy when they refuse to explain choices or dismiss every objection as hostility to creativity. Taxpayers may then see independence as an absence of accountability, undermining support for the wider principle of publicly funded artistic experimentation. Funding decisions should be independent, transparent and open to reasoned public challenge. Independent panels should explain funding criteria and consider reasoned objections, protecting experimentation without suggesting that public institutions owe taxpayers no account of their choices. Funding should protect independent artistic judgement while explaining selection criteria and allowing reasoned criticism, rather than equating every objection with a demand for censorship.

Supporters rightly resist making popularity a funding condition, while opponents rightly require accountability for public money; independent selection with reasoned explanation protects artistic freedom more convincingly than dismissing criticism or withdrawing support whenever offence occurs.

paragraphs.quote: Public institutions can lose trust if they dismiss all criticism as hostility to artistic freedom. Funding bodies can lose legitimacy when they refuse to explain choices or dismiss every objection as hostility to creativity. Taxpayers may then see independence as an absence of accountability, undermining support for the wider principle of publicly funded artistic experimentation. Funding decisions should be independent, transparent and open to reasoned public challenge. Independent panels should explain funding criteria and consider reasoned objections, protecting experimentation without suggesting that public institutions owe taxpayers no account of their choices. Funding should protect independent artistic judgement while explaining selection criteria and allowing reasoned criticism, rather than equating every objection with a demand for censorship.
paragraphs.why: Quyết định độc lập giảm can thiệp chính trị; minh bạch và quyền phản biện giữ trách nhiệm công. Không nên dùng tự do nghệ thuật để miễn mọi giải trình ngân sách.

review: Task Response: Kết luận trả lại cả hai cách nhìn và quyết định của người viết; không cần chia đều số câu nhưng phải giải thích thực chất cả hai phía. Đã xử lý phản biện “Public institutions can lose trust if they dismiss all criticism as hostility to artistic freedom.” chưa?

options: I completely support allowing public funding for art that offends some taxpayers in every circumstance, regardless of its consequences.

I favour protecting challenging art from a taxpayer veto, but agree with opponents that public institutions owe an explanation of artistic value and selection procedures rather than an automatic defence of controversy.
The issue of allowing public funding for art that offends some taxpayers is very important in modern society and has many different opinions.
